To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
every social practice is a signifying practice and that it obeys the laws of signifying practices.
the signifier, insofar as it signifies, constitutes the law of any sign-system, including that of social practice, which is thus a system of signifiers.
every social practice is a signifying practice, that the signifying practice is a language, and that the language is a system.
In summary, our research is concerned with
discovering the law of signifying practices.
the fact that every social practice is articulated in a language and, consequently, is subject to the laws of signification.
the fact that every social system, every social practice (whether religious, political, economic, or artistic) signifies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
semiotics has discovered that social practices are signifying practices.
the system and the speaking subject are inextricably interwoven.
every social practice is a signifying practice, that is to say, a practice which is articulated in a signifying order, in a language.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
semiotics has discovered that the signifying process is a social process, that it is the social process, and that it is the process by means of which society is constituted as society.
we have discovered the ‘linguistic’ nature of social practices.
the semiotic discovery is a discovery of language, of the symbolic, as the law governing social practice.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we need to think about the relationship between the system and the speaking subject.
the semiotic approach to social practices has a double advantage.
the semiotic and the social are not opposed but rather coextensive and co-constitutive.
